title.narrative: Promote Sustainable Urban Development through “Global Sustainable Development Award for Cities” (“Shanghai Award”) and Related Activities (Phase I and Phase II)

description.narrative:
Year 2021 ushers the Decade of Action to accelerate the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals and deliver the 2030 Agenda. However, global efforts to date have been insufficient to deliver the transformations we anticipate. Due to the unprecedented pandemic COVID-19, achieving the SDGs has become even more challenging. Immense political will, ambitious actions and a shared vision by stakeholder around the world are required to accelerate the global efforts to address the world’s most pressing challenges and realise the SDGs.
As a major global trend in the contemporary world, sustainable urbanization presents massive opportunities in transforming people’s lives and reducing inequalities. Cities are a major transformative force as innovators and implementors the SDGs. To grasp advance local actions, it is important to further incentivise cities, to promote the shared vision of sustainable urban development through global advocacy, cooperation and recognition of excellence among international community.
UN-Habitat repositions itself as a Centre of Excellence and innovation, which acts as a multiplier in the exchange of knowledge, experience and best practice in getting cities right. In 2020, UN-Habitat has also launched its flagship programme “SDG Cities”, a global initiative that unleashes the potential of cities to accelerate sustainable development by linking data to policy and planning actions and recognizing the achievements of cities through the SDG Cities certification. UN-Habitat is also leading the process to build a UN system-wide index for cities, the Global Urban Monitoring Framework (GUMF), to provide a reliable, internally comparable and recognized data instrument for cities and other urban practitioners.
In this context, the minister and vice minister of the Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development of People’s Republic of China (MOHURD) and the mayor of Shanghai Municipality have had several meetings with the Executive Director of UN-Habitat to discuss the potential collaborations that can enhance the local actions for achieving the SDGs globally. As a result, UN-Habitat, MOHURD and Shanghai Municipal Commission of Housing and Urban-Rural Development and Management have agreed to work together to conduct feasibility studies on establishing a global platform that strengthens the international cooperation and experience sharing among cities in China and other countries, including the Belt and Road partner countries. It is also envisioned to strengthen the platform with practical monitoring tools that are adapted based on GUMF as well as knowledge sharing opportunities and products.
To achieve this goal, this project includes three interlinked initiatives, i.e. (1) conducting feasibility studies on setting up “Global Sustainable Development Award for Cities” (“Shanghai Award”) and incentivizing cities to accelerate the implementation of the SDGs and New Urban Agenda through the annual selection and celebration of winning cities of the Shanghai Award; (2) conducting research on developing the “Global Urban Monitoring Framework – Shanghai Adapted Index” (hereinafter referred to as “Shanghai Adapted Index”) and promoting the application of the Shanghai Adapted Index among piloting cities; (3) strengthening “Shanghai Manual” annual report that incorporates the results of Shanghai Award, Shanghai Adapted Index and SDG Cities.
